messages:
olivia-eng: quick heads-up — found a misconfigured ClusterRoleBinding on kube1 that effectively gives the gpu-scheduler serviceaccount cross-namespace exec and pod access. also seeing intermittent KMS decrypt failures tied to recent deploys. :(

jessica-sec: can you paste the binding and any logs?

olivia-eng: pasted from kube1: ```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: gpu-scheduler-global
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: gpu-scheduler-role
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: gpu-scheduler
  # missing namespace here — this made it cluster-scoped unintentionally
```

raj-sre: ouch. missing namespace on the subject is the classic footgun. that SA now has cluster-wide rights for that role. :eyes:

kevin-ops: what permissions does `gpu-scheduler-role` grant? `pods/exec`? `pods/create`?

olivia-eng: it includes: `pods/exec`, `pods/attach`, `pods/create` (for helper sidecars), and `pods/portforward`. intended scope was single-namespace scheduler workload.

jessica-sec: immediate mitigation: replace ClusterRoleBinding with namespaced RoleBinding for the scheduler namespace and revoke the cluster binding. we should also rotate the SA tokens used by the scheduler.

raj-sre: agreed. proposed steps: 1) create namespaced Role + RoleBinding in `gpu-scheduler` ns; 2) create short-lived token via TokenRequest for scheduler pods (or use projected service account tokens) and enforce impersonation where possible; 3) remove the ClusterRoleBinding; 4) run audit scan to find other bindings missing namespaces.

kevin-ops: i'll prepare a migration job. rough `kubectl` commands:```bash
kubectl create role gpu-scheduler-role -n gpu-scheduler --verb=create,exec,attach,portforward --resource=pods
kubectl create rolebinding gpu-scheduler-binding -n gpu-scheduler --role=gpu-scheduler-role --serviceaccount=gpu-scheduler:gpu-scheduler
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding gpu-scheduler-global
```

jessica-sec: also add a test: `kubectl auth can-i exec pods --as=system:serviceaccount:gpu-scheduler:gpu-scheduler -n other-namespace` should return `no`. Add that to the CI policy.

olivia-eng: on the KMS side — deploy logs show `KMS: decryption error: permissionDenied` ~1-2% of deploys in the last 48h. audit-bot attached the CloudKMS log ids.

audit-bot: logged events: [CLOUDKMS_DECRYPT: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/deploy-key/cryptoKeys/deploy-key - 1890012360, 1890012392]

jessica-sec: if the SA that calls KMS is rotated or missing the `cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` role in some namespaces (we use KMS via sidecar), that could cause intermittent failures. correlate KMS request principal with pod/serviceaccount in the cluster audit logs.

raj-sre: quick correlation query I ran: cluster audit shows TokenRequest usage at 1890012355 from pod `deploy-worker-7` then a KMS decrypt error at 1890012356. looks like that pod was still using an old cached token that KMS rejected due to IAM policy change.

kevin-ops: remediation plan: 1) rotate gpu-scheduler SA tokens / restart pods to pick up new tokens; 2) ensure KMS IAM grants `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to the correct GCP service account mapped to the Kubernetes SA via workload identity (or annotate if using GKE). 3) add explicit request metadata to KMS calls (`purpose=deploy`) so audit can link them.

jessica-sec: long-term: write a mutating admission webhook that rejects ClusterRoleBindings whose subjects omit namespace for ServiceAccount kind, unless a specific allowlist exists. run a one-off repair tool to convert cluster-scoped SA subjects into explicit namespaced bindings and produce a reconciliation report.

olivia-eng: i'll open a PR with the migration job + CI check and schedule a canary rollout to staging first. tagging @kevin-ops for the KMS IAM audit. thanks all. :+1:

kevin-ops: on it. i'll also add an alert on `cloudkms` permission errors so we catch this faster next time.

jessica-sec: follow-up todo: add a short runbook entry for this class of misconfig (rbac.subjects namespace missing) and include quick detection queries for audit logs.

raj-sre: noted — i'll add the `kubectl auth can-i` tests to the cluster-e2e suite and kick off the repair job once olivia's PR is ready.
